snippet.title: After Renee Good’s Killing, a Snowball, and Then Tear Gas | FRONTLINE + @ProPublica
snippet.description:
Five days after an ICE agent fatally shot activist Renee Good, @frontline & @ProPublica filmed as tensions ran high in the Minneapolis neighborhood where Good had been killed. A protester threw a snowball. Federal agents responded with tear gas, pepper balls and pepper spray, hitting members of the reporting team in the face. "We see just use of excessive force after use of excess force," said a former DOJ official who looked at the team's footage.

snippet.title: Immigration Under President Trump’s First Term | Kids Caught in the Crackdown (full documentary)
snippet.description:
With @AssociatedPress, an Emmy Award-winning examination into conditions inside federally-funded shelter programs for detained migrant children and the lasting impact on kids who were held in U.S. government custody. (Aired 2019)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

Detention of migrant children climbed to historic levels during President Donald Trump’s first term. Drawing on confidential government data obtained by @AssociatedPress, "Caught in the Crackdown” revealed how many migrant kids were being held — and where — at any given time.

With unique access — including inside a “tender age” shelter that held some of the youngest children in government custody — the film illuminated what happened when a child apprehended by Customs and Border Protection was handed over to the Department of Health and Human Services, known as HHS. The documentary examined how changes in policies for how sponsors were vetted meant kids were held in government custody for longer and longer periods, and in larger and larger numbers.

In 2020, the documentary was honored with a News Emmy in the “Outstanding Continuing Coverage of a News Story in a Newsmagazine” category. 

“Kids Caught in the Crackdown” was a FRONTLINE production with Five O’Clock Films in partnership with The Associated Press. The writers, producers and directors were Daffodil Altan and Andrés Cediel. The co-producer was Sasha Joelle Achilli. The reporters were Garance Burke and Martha Mendoza. The correspondent was Daffodil Altan. The senior producer was Frank Koughan. The international investigations editor for AP was Ron Nixon. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is  Raney Aronson-Rath.

snippet.title: NYC's Soccer Mecca | World's Pitch: Flushing Meadows
snippet.description:
Welcome to the "Mecca of football". Tucked away in Queens, Flushing Meadows is the historic temple of amateur soccer in New York City, but its fields weren't always guaranteed. 

In this documentary, we look at the legacy of Flushing Meadows through the eyes of Dino Raul Dominguez del Salto, the president of Liga Deportiva Estudiantil and an NYC Hall of Fame inductee. Arriving in America in 1968, Dino and a community of passionate immigrant players fought for their right to play. Facing a lack of official pitches and operating without permits, they brought their own goalposts, fixed the fields themselves, and even took their protests directly to City Hall.  Today, this iconic park serves as a second home for generations of families—a vibrant subculture built on brotherhood, drive, and an unyielding love for the beautiful game. But as immigration pressures and shifting generations alter the league's landscape, a new question arises: who will step up to carry the torch?

Stars: Historians, archival footage, eyewitness accounts
Genre: Documentary, History, War
Country: Germany
Language: English

Synopsis:
In War of Annihilation, the fifth episode of On the Edge of the Abyss, the conflict reaches a new level of brutality as Nazi Germany launches its massive invasion of the Soviet Union. What unfolds on the Eastern Front is not just a war for territory, but a war driven by ideology — one that aims at total destruction.

Through powerful archival footage and expert analysis, the documentary reveals the scale and intensity of Operation Barbarossa, one of the largest military offensives in history. Entire regions are devastated, and millions of soldiers and civilians are drawn into a conflict marked by extreme violence and suffering.

As the front stretches across vast landscapes, the realities of war become increasingly brutal: mass executions, scorched earth tactics, and relentless fighting under harsh conditions. This episode exposes the true nature of a war without limits — where survival itself becomes uncertain.

snippet.title: Tracking Suspected Members of the Pakistani Taliban | Taliban Hunters (full documentary) | FRONTLINE
snippet.description:
Inside a counterterrorism police unit in Karachi, Pakistan, dedicated to tracking down suspected members of the Pakistani Taliban. (Aired 2015)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the nearly five years since the Taliban seized control of Afghanistan, there’s been a dramatic increase in attacks within neighboring Pakistan by the militant group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, commonly called the Pakistani Taliban or TTP. Pakistan has accused Taliban-controlled Afghanistan of harboring the group and enabling it to launch cross-border attacks, which the Afghan government denies — and in recent weeks, the fight between the two countries escalated into what Pakistan’s government called “open war.”

Against this volatile backdrop, FRONTLINE’s 2015 documentary “Taliban Hunters” offers relevant history on TTP and Pakistani security forces’ fight against it. This short documentary went inside a Karachi-based counterterrorism police unit dedicated to tracking down Taliban suspects. 

As the documentary reported, TTP first emerged in 2007 and used to have only a small, underground presence in Karachi, Pakistan’s largest city. But by the time the documentary aired, the group had been gaining ground in the city of over 20 million people, and carrying out suicide bombings and targeted assassinations there.

The film documented how the unit carried out raids to take suspected TTP members into custody. It also explored human rights groups’ allegations that Karachi authorities were abusing militants captured in the city’s fight against terrorism. Amid TTP’s current resurgence, “Taliban Hunters” is an illuminating snapshot of where the fight against them stood in one large city back in 2015, and how the group operated.

“Taliban Hunters” is directed and reported by Mobeen Azhar and produced by Jamie Doran. The senior producer for FRONTLINE is Dan Edge.
